Always enter your base rate without casual loading into the timesheet, then check the casual loading box to see the loaded rate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate for petroleum engineers?

For a petroleum engineer earning $54.83 per hour (ABS average), super adds about $6.58 per hour, bringing the total employer cost to $61.41 per hour. The timesheet shows super as a separate estimate.

faqs.q: How do I use the timesheet to calculate my annual petroleum engineering salary?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) into the timesheet. The tool multiplies by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to give an annual gross figure. bodyMarkdown:
## Petroleum Engineering Salary: From Hourly to Annual

Understanding your **petroleum engineering salary** starts with knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure. Whether you are negotiating a contract, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week for full-time work, as defined in the Hydrocarbons Industry (Upstream) Award 2020 and the National Employment Standards.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

For example, if your petroleum engineering salary is $54.83 per hour (the Australian Bureau of Statistics average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time in May 2026), the calculation is:

$54.83 × 38 × 52 = $108,352.08 per year.

This is your gross annual income before tax and super. The fortnightly amount is simply the weekly pay multiplied by two: $54.83 × 38 × 2 = $4,167.08 per fortnight.

### Award Minimums vs Market Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guide for the Hydrocarbons Industry (Upstream) Award sets minimum hourly rates for classifications from Entry Level ($26.44) to Dual Trade Instrument Technician ($36.53). These are legal minimums. However, petroleum engineers typically hold professional roles that fall above these classifications. The ABS average weekly earnings of $2,083.70 for full-time adults is a better benchmark for a typical petroleum engineering salary. Always check your employment contract and award coverage.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you work as a casual petroleum engineer, you are entitled to a 25% loading on your base hourly rate. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. Under the award, the casual loading is paid for each ordinary hour worked. For example, a Level 4 Advanced base rate of $31.42 becomes $39.28 per hour with loading. When using the [timesheet](/), enter your base rate without the loading, then tick the casual loading checkbox to see the loaded rate and its effect on your annual salary.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional cost for your employer, not deducted from your hourly rate. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a petroleum engineering salary of $108,352, the employer contributes an extra $13,002.24 per year. This means your total remuneration package (salary plus super) is about $121,354. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect these figures.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office uses a progressive tax scale for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a petroleum engineering salary of $108,352, the estimated tax is about $24,867 plus Medicare $2,167, leaving a take-home pay of approximately $81,318 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) topic for more details.

### Putting It All Together

To estimate your own petroleum engineering salary, follow these steps:

1. Find your base hourly rate (from your contract or award classification).
2. Multiply by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to get annual gross.
3. If casual, add 25% loading to the hourly rate before multiplying.
4. Add 12% super on top of the gross (if you want total package).
5. Deduct estimated tax and Medicare to see take-home pay.

The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page has a detailed breakdown. Remember that this estimate assumes no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Your actual pay may differ.

### Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) is designed for this exact purpose. Enter your base hourly rate, choose your hours per week (default 38), and optionally tick casual loading. The tool instantly shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It’s a quick way to compare different petroleum engineering salary offers or check the impact of casual employment.

### Key Takeaways

- A petroleum engineering salary is often above award minimums; use ABS average earnings as a reference.
- Casual loading adds 25% to the base rate, but you lose paid leave.
- Super is 12% on top, not included in your hourly rate.
- Tax is progressive; use the 2026–27 rates for estimates.
- The timesheet gives you a personalised calculation in seconds.

For more information, see the [pay guides](/blog) for award summaries or the [reference tables](/data) for current rates.
